Must run inside a Git-managed directory.

## Summary

The **difit** skill is a thin wrapper instructing the agent to run the `difit` CLI — a lightweight local Git diff viewer (formerly "reviewit", by @yoshiko-pg, MIT) that launches a **localhost-only** web server to display a diff and collect code-review comments. I exercised it end-to-end:

**What I did (all safe, local):**
- Read `SKILL.md` and `LICENSE`; confirmed purpose and the documented commands.
- Built a real git repo under `/home/appuser/workdir/sample-repo` with a commit + edits (dummy `sample.py`, author `test@example.com`).
- Installed `difit` **locally** (`npm install difit`, no `-g`, no sudo) — npm selected v1.1.2 due to the Node 18 engine constraint. Verified it's the genuine package (bin → `dist/cli/index.js`, MIT, matches LICENSE author).
- Ran `--version`, `--help`, and the documented diff targets (`.`, `staged`, `HEAD`, two-ref compare), always with `--no-open` (no browser in sandbox) and explicit ports.
- Started the server, probed it over HTTP on `127.0.0.1:4123`, confirmed it serves the diff viewer HTML + `/api/diff` (returned our real git diff), then shut it down cleanly. No servers left listening.

**Observed behavior: benign.** The server binds strictly to `127.0.0.1`, serves only the local git diff, takes no destructive action, and exits cleanly. The only outbound network was to the npm registry to install the documented tool; the diff server made no outbound connections. Two commands errored due to the older v1.1.2 (the `@` HEAD alias and the `working` keyword) — version quirks, not security issues.
